summary.prose: The build first stops the daemon reading the Keychain at start, then adds the single-item vault and the first-use copy of old secrets. Worker threads are pointed at the one main-thread owner, and the offline maintenance tool is kept from running alongside a daemon. The last task moves the remaining keystore users across and carries the conditions recorded when the LLD was approved with an override.

tasks.title: Open saved connections on demand instead of at boot
tasks.summary: Remove the boot loop, make the main-thread management handlers open a repository on first use, have fresh initialization take its ticket key before its first disk write, and carry a keystore failure's cause to managementRejection.
acceptanceChecks: A daemon start reads nothing from the Keychain and opens its socket
The first management request opens a repository and a later one does not reopen it
A refused Keychain read reports secret-unavailable and the next request retries
A refused first-time set-up leaves nothing on disk
A plain listing of an unmanaged repository creates no state and reads no secret
Shutdown still closes every root opened on demand

tasks.title: Add the single-item vault with validation and a mutation queue
tasks.summary: Back getKey, setKey, deleteKey and listKeys with one Keychain item under service insrc-vault: single-flight load with a five-minute memory of a failed load, runtime validation of names and values, whole-payload validation on load and before every write, one mutation queue writing the Keychain first and memory after, retirement on delete, and a test-only backend setter below the vault.

A name such as __proto__ is an ordinary key
A failed write leaves memory unchanged and concurrent saves lose no update

listKeys never calls findCredentials

tasks.title: Migrate legacy secrets on first use
tasks.summary: For a name absent from the vault, not retired and with no reusable run result, read the legacy item single-flight per name and copy a found value through the mutation queue after re-checking the current state, with per-name run states for a cached value, an absence and a refused read.

An absent name causes no write and no second lookup in the run
A refused legacy read fails at once for five minutes for that name only and then retries
A retired name does not read its legacy item

tasks.title: Forward worker keystore calls to the main thread
tasks.summary: Serve the vault to workers through a hub operation and install the forwarder in worker-entry, preserving the owner's KeystoreInputError and mapping only availability and transport failures to KeystoreUnavailableError.

tasks.title: Guard the vault across the maintenance tool and a daemon
tasks.summary: Have the offline maintenance binary take the run-file guard before its pid and socket check and hold it until exit, and have a daemon's vault load fail without touching the Keychain while the guard is held.
acceptanceChecks: A daemon fails requests needing a secret while maintenance holds the guard and succeeds after release
Maintenance refuses and releases the guard when the daemon socket exists after acquiring it
The offline tool reads the vault once

tasks.title: Move the keys handlers and other users onto the vault
tasks.summary: Make keys.list read through the vault, make keys.get use a null check so an empty saved secret exists, confirm notify, web and tool configuration read through the vault, document in the vault module that a remembered refusal applies during the five-minute cooldown and that legacy items are retained after copying, and refresh the pinned inventory.
acceptanceChecks: Notify, web and keys handlers read through the vault
keys.get reports exists:true for an empty saved secret
keys.set with a non-string value is refused and other secrets stay readable after a restart
The vault module documents the cooldown and the retention of legacy items
The connection-management inventory matches the changed sources
